safety_verdicts.content: Patient has also been vomiting, with no blood in the vomit.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes vomiting but does not document the key associated negative of no blood in vomit (hematemesis denied).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document denial of hematemesis removes an important negative red-flag in an acute GI presentation, which can affect risk stratification and subsequent triage if symptoms evolve. Most often it results in additional questioning, but it can also blur recognition of possible GI bleeding.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a loss of appetite.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Loss of appetite is not documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Loss of appetite is a common associated symptom in gastroenteritis and is not typically a key discriminator for emergent pathology on its own. Omission mainly reduces completeness of symptom characterization.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting absence of other unwell contacts can slightly affect assessment of infectious exposure and counseling, but it rarely changes immediate management in a straightforward diarrhea/vomiting case. The likely impact is minor clarification later.
